newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador president overturns Congress tax bill.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador president overturns Congress tax bill.

text.p: Ecuador's president has vetoed congressional changes to a tax bill and is set to return the legislation to Congress for approval with his amendments.
The government's original bill proposed an increase in value added tax on soft drinks to 12 percent, but Congress lowered that to eight percent.

President Fabian Alarcon is now proposing a 10 percent tax. If VAT of just eight percent tax were introduced it would cost the government some 2,200 million sucres ($544,500) in lost revenues a year, Congressional sources said.
Alarcon took advantage of typing errors in the congressional amendments to stop them. He is expected to confirm his veto in a Congressional session Wednesday, Congressional sources said.

"A partial veto was introduced Tuesday and when Congress received a call from the presidency saying there were typing errors that had to be corrected, Congress suspended its treatment of the law," a congressional source told Reuters.
A second disagreement centered on whether a 10 percent tax on cable television should be a special consumption tax or a value added tax as the president wants.
The government is set on raising taxes in an effort to cover the budget deficit, which is expected to reach six percent of gross domestic product this year.
